title: Piano Movers in Anaheim | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Piano movers in Anaheim, billed by the hour: four movers, a padded board and straps, with the curb, the gate and the auto court checked before move day.
heroSubtitle: Four movers, a piano board and straps, one hourly clock — the instrument loads first and rides tied to the truck wall.

faq.question: Can you move just the piano, or does it have to be part of a bigger move?
faq.answer: Either works, and the structure is the same both ways. A piano goes with a crew of four, a flat $200 piano charge and a three-hour minimum, whether it travels alone or leaves with the rest of the furniture. Nothing about the instrument creates a second booking with its own minimum.

faq.question: What does a piano move in Anaheim cost?
faq.answer: Four movers with a truck run $199 an hour in cash or $209 by card Monday through Thursday, and $215 or $225 Friday through Sunday. Add the $200 piano charge, a $30 fuel fee, and a $50 deposit that comes straight off the bill. Drive time doubles past ten miles, and the minimum becomes four hours at thirty miles or more from our base.

faq.question: Where will the truck park on my street?
faq.answer: Anaheim treats a vehicle over 22 feet long as oversized and keeps it off public streets, with an exemption for active loading and unloading at the curb immediately adjacent to the building, or within 400 feet when that curb cannot be used. Send a photo of your block when you book and the driver plans the closest legal spot.

faq.question: My community is gated. What do you need from me?
faq.answer: The names of the four movers and a description of the truck, passed to the association or front desk before the date. In the guard-gated pockets of Anaheim Hills that gate is the only way in, so an approval that lands the morning of the move costs you clock time. If the building wants a certificate of insurance, that is $50.

faq.question: Do you tune the instrument afterwards?
faq.answer: No. We lift, protect, carry, place and level the instrument on its castor cups, and that is where our work ends. Tuning and appraisal are separate trades, and we do not keep instruments in storage, so book a technician directly once the piano is standing in its new room.

faq.question: Stairs, a slope or a lift — what changes?
faq.answer: The plan changes, not the rate card. Steps and grade are worked with the board across the slope rather than down it, and in a building with a lift the piano rides up alone with two movers while the other two receive it. All of it is billed as the same hourly time, which is why the walk length matters more than the mileage on most jobs.
